title: Power, fuse, battery and lightning safety
blurb: Spot the shock, fire and battery hazards in a station, and know where fuses, arresters and grounds belong.

T0A01.why: Shorting a battery's terminals sends enormous current through the short: **burns, fire or explosion**.
T0A01.trap: 12 V across your hands is too low to shock you, and RF can't make electrolyte emit gas.

T0A02.why: Body current heats tissue, disrupts cells and causes involuntary muscle contractions: **all three**.

T0A03.why: In US 120 V cable, **black is hot**. White is neutral and green or bare is the equipment ground.

T0A04.why: A fuse **opens the circuit on overload**, removing power before wiring overheats.
T0A04.trap: A fuse doesn't filter ripple, and it doesn't limit current to prevent shocks.

T0A05.why: A 20 A fuse lets 20 A flow in wiring meant for 5 A. The wire overheats and can start a **fire**.
T0A05.trap: A bigger fuse blows less often, which is exactly the problem.

T0A06.why: Three-wire cords, a common safety ground and discharged capacitors **each** reduce shock risk.

T0A07.why: Mount the arrester on a **grounded panel where feed lines enter** the building, so surges are diverted before they come inside.

T0A08.why: A fuse or breaker goes **in series with the hot conductor only**. Opening the hot wire de-energizes the circuit.
T0A08.trap: Parallel would short out the supply. Fusing neutral can leave the hot wire live.

T0A09.why: Bond all external grounds together with **heavy wire or strap** so they rise and fall together during a strike.

T0A10.why: Charging or discharging an unprotected battery too fast makes it **overheat and out-gas**.

T0A11.why: Filter capacitors **keep their charge** after power is removed. Discharge them before touching anything inside.

T0A12.why: A voltmeter and its leads must be **rated for the voltages** measured, or they can fail and shock you.
T0A12.trap: A meter should have high, not low, impedance, and nothing is grounded through it.
